targetText: The consanguine family is extinct. Even the most primitive peoples known to history provide no demonstrable instance of it. But that it must have existed, we are compelled to admit
summary: The consanguine (generation-based) family stage is no longer practiced anywhere today, but its historical existence is proven by ancient kinship naming systems preserved in language.
context: Engels shows how anthropologists deduce prehistoric social stages. Even after actual marriage customs change, old kinship terms linger in language, allowing historians to reconstruct earliest human family forms.
